methodology: MVP: Sleeper player search rank + actual league production (when available) + roster fit + starting-lineup impact.
headline: Blueballs Adds the Biggest Bat in a Three-for-Three Swap
verdict: Blueballs is the current winner, with the stronger B grade and a clear edge in overall trade value.
summary: This is a quantity-for-quality exchange, and the scoreboard leans Kane’s way. Blueballs turns Mooney, Etienne, and Bigsby into Deebo Samuel, Breece Hall, and Chase Brown, moving from a 132.1 package to a 176.2 package on the supplied heuristic values. Chase Brown’s 15-point season average and 17.8 recent average headline the deal, while Hall brings a 13.1 season average and a search rank of 27. Cooper’s C+ grade is rescued by strong roster fit, especially with only five wide receivers, but the lineup-impact score remains modest at 68. Kane’s 8-6 Blueballs gets the better value swing, though both teams share that record and neither side is guaranteed anything.

sides.analysis: Kane’s Blueballs gets the deal’s strongest package, led by Chase Brown’s 86.6 value, search rank of 16, 15-point season average, and 17.8 recent average. Breece Hall adds a 75.2 value, 27 search rank, and 13.1 season average, while Deebo Samuel offers a 13 recent average after a 9 season average. The return totals 176.2 on the supplied heuristic scale, well above what Blueballs sends out. The fit is solid rather than perfect: Kane already has Kyren Williams, Brian Thomas, and Mike Evans among his top players. Still, an 83.4 overall score and B grade make this a substantial upgrade.
sides.bestReason: Chase Brown supplies the clearest production and market-value edge, with Hall adding another high-value running back.
sides.biggestRisk: The 76 lineup-impact score shows that the large paper-value gain may not translate into an equally large starting-lineup boost.

sides.analysis: Cooper’s Jack MeHoff receives three players for three players, but the package is lighter on the supplied heuristic values at 132.1. Travis Etienne brings the best incoming value at 64.7, with a 7.1 season average and 8.9 recent average. Darnell Mooney adds a 51.5 value and 11.5 season average, while Tank Bigsby checks in at 50.5 value, 7.3 season average, and 5.9 recent average. The roster-fit score of 87.7 is the bright spot: Cooper has five wide receivers and four running backs, so the incoming mix addresses roster construction. The C+ grade reflects that fit, but the 68 lineup-impact score keeps the ceiling restrained.
sides.bestReason: The deal fits Cooper’s roster better than the raw values suggest, particularly by adding a wide receiver to a five-WR room.
sides.biggestRisk: Cooper gives up Deebo, Hall, and Brown’s 176.2 package value for a 132.1 return, leaving a sizable talent gap to overcome.
